summary: Inheritance makes a new class that starts with all the fields and methods of an existing class. You add new methods or override old ones in the child class.
notes: class HonorsStudent(Student) names the parent class in parentheses.
super().__init__(name, scores) must run, or self.name and self.scores are never set.
super().describe() calls the parent's version of a method you have overridden.
pitfall: Leaving out super().__init__(...) in the child's __init__ causes AttributeError: 'HonorsStudent' object has no attribute 'scores' when average() runs.
